comment: The patient_profile briefing, as a text template document. It is what jets/agentic/briefing/prose renders, expressed in the notation of plan section 10 of projects/agentic_ai/plan/phase8_plan.md, and jets/agentic/template is the engine that reads it. This file is the ONE copy: BA.2 inlines it into patient_profile_template.pc.json's text_templates array and TestTheShippedPipelineCarriesThisDocument compares the two. Every element below carries the argument for its predicate, because a predicate is a line of logic and the code it reproduces has a comment where this has none.

elements.comment: The notice, and the engine has no idea what it is. Section 10.7: two of Render's three refusals become assertions in the document and one leaves the engine. This is the first of the two. The require fires on blank rendered text and not only on an absent property (I-645), which is what prose.Render does - it compares the trimmed disclaimer with the empty string - so a whitespace-only notice is refused here as it is there.
elements.text: {{Briefing_Disclaimer require 'the briefing entity carries no Briefing_Disclaimer; the notice is asserted unconditionally by BP_Disclaimer10 and the rendered artefact is notice, rule, prose in that order'}}

elements.comment: The rule, which is 68 hyphens verbatim from prose.go and is inside width, so it is never wrapped. A literal paragraph: the second of the two most briefing-shaped things in the artefact, and the notation needed no concept for either.

The body, and the fallback is this group's rather than the document's. prose.Render puts the notice and the rule ABOVE the empty sentence, so a briefing with no activity is notice, rule, sentence rather than sentence alone; a flat element list cannot express that, because the notice always emits and a document-level fallback would never fire (section 10.6).
elements.empty: No claims activity on record for this member.

elements.comment: renderBody reaches the empty sentence by two predicates that are not equivalent (F1149), and this nested group is the first of them: both counts zero is an early return BEFORE any element runs, so it suppresses the conditions element too. Section 10.9 writes it as a conjunct on the conditions element alone, which is wrong for the medications element - a Pharmacy_Event_Count of 0 beside a populated event list and no medical activity emits Medications: there and the empty sentence in the code. A group is the honest shape: the guard is written once, it covers all three elements, and the outer group's empty still fires because a group that emits nothing leaves its parent with no emitting child. The second predicate - every element produced nothing - is the outer group's empty, so both are kept and neither is a special case. The two count[] disjuncts are countOf's fallback: see the medical element below.
elements.when: Medical_Event_Count > 0 or (Medical_Event_Count == '' and has_Briefing_Medical_Events[]|count > 0) or Pharmacy_Event_Count > 0 or (Pharmacy_Event_Count == '' and has_Briefing_Pharmacy_Events[]|count > 0)

elements.comment: Elements 1 and 2 of section 1.10.3 in one paragraph: how much and how recently, then what the last contact was. Three decisions are transcribed rather than invented. latest_by is applied to the EVENTS and not to Latest_Service_Date, because the briefing-level extremum is a date and this clause needs the encounter it belongs to. The care setting is verbatim in a labelled clause and is not folded into a fluent sentence, because the article rule produces at a telehealth over the 52 place-of-service descriptions. And with supplies the guard that P7 section 1.10.6 forgot (F1148): a span scoped to a chain yielding nothing emits nothing, so the sketch's Most recent contact: , 5 May. cannot happen. The two Medical_Event_Count branches are I-621, decided here rather than inherited: countOf prefers the projected count and falls back to the length of the list it counts, and dropping the fallback does not cost a sentence - it makes a member with events and no count render No claims activity on record, which is an affirmative false statement and is the failure mode the prefixed-entity refusal exists to prevent. The reproduction is exact for an absent or blank count and not for one present and non-numeric, which needs a negation the notation does not have.
elements.text: {{if Medical_Event_Count != ''}}{{Medical_Event_Count|words|sentence}} medical {{Medical_Event_Count|plural: 'visit'}}{{end}}{{if Medical_Event_Count == ''}}{{has_Briefing_Medical_Events[]|count|words|sentence}} medical {{has_Briefing_Medical_Events[]|count|plural: 'visit'}}{{end}} on record{{if Earliest_Service_Date|d_MMMM != '' and Latest_Service_Date|d_MMMM_yyyy != ''}}, between {{Earliest_Service_Date|d_MMMM}} and {{Latest_Service_Date|d_MMMM_yyyy}}{{end}}. {{with has_Briefing_Medical_Events[]|latest_by: Service_Date}}Most recent contact: {{if Care_Setting != ''}}{{Care_Setting}}, {{end}}{{Service_Date|d_MMMM}}.{{end}}

elements.comment: Element 3, and it is third rather than first on purpose: a briefing that opens with a diagnosis list reads like a clinical handover, and under A section 8's read-aloud test the first line is the line most likely to be spoken. Do not improve the order. The parenthesised code is stripped in the prose and stays on the entity - it exists so a checker can match a whole string exactly, and it is noise to a member. The gate is the rendered list rather than count > 0, because elementConditions filters values that are empty AFTER the code is stripped and only then asks whether anything is left: a Condition_Summary of one blank string gives count 1 and would emit Conditions on record: with nothing after it. join skips an empty item here (I-624), so the gate and the text are the same chain and there is no rule about what precedes the join.

Element 4, the one element a representative can act on with no judgement at all. It reads the components and never the joined Medication value, which is the second of Render's assertions moved into the document (I-544): recovering the drug name from the joined value would encode AT.6's separator in a second place. The gate is the LIST and not Pharmacy_Event_Count, because elementMedications returns early only when the count is not positive AND the list is empty, so guarding on the count would emit Medications: . for a count with no list. Maintenance is matched against both cases, which is I-622 decided here: strings.EqualFold over a trimmed value is true for y and for Y and for nothing else, so the disjunction is that function written out rather than an approximation of it, and section 10.4's case-sensitive == is left alone for Care_Setting's sake. The second Fill_Count branch is fillCount's fallback, I-621 again: the projected count wins and the fill dates are the same fact counted rather than a different one. The individual fill dates are not listed - the count and the latest carry the whole of what this element does, and three dates per drug is length for a member on four maintenance drugs.
elements.text: Medications: {{each has_Briefing_Pharmacy_Events[] sep: '; ' last: '; and '}}{{Drug_Name require 'a pharmacy event of the briefing carries no Drug_Name; the renderer reads the components of a medication and never the joined Medication value, so that the separator AT.6 writes lives in one place (I-544)'}}{{if Maintenance == 'Y' or Maintenance == 'y'}}, a maintenance medication{{end}}{{if Fill_Count != ''}}, {{Fill_Count|words}} {{Fill_Count|plural: 'fill'}}{{if Fill_Date[]|max|d_MMMM != ''}}, most recently {{Fill_Date[]|max|d_MMMM}}{{end}}{{end}}{{if Fill_Count == '' and Fill_Date[]|count > 0}}, {{Fill_Date[]|count|words}} {{Fill_Date[]|count|plural: 'fill'}}{{if Fill_Date[]|max|d_MMMM != ''}}, most recently {{Fill_Date[]|max|d_MMMM}}{{end}}{{end}}{{end}}.
